newsitem.title: USA: Immunex settles suit with Cistron.
newsitem.headline: Immunex settles suit with Cistron.

text.p: Immunex Corp said it settled a lawsuit brought against it by Cistron Biotechnology Inc alleging the theft of intellectual property.

The claims were made against Immunex and two former officers of Immunex. Under terms of the settlement, the defendants will pay Cistron a total of $21 million -- payable $11 million on November 15; three installments of $3 million each on November 15 of each of the following three years beginning in 1997; and $1 million on November 15, 2000.
Immunex will also assign certain IL-1 beta patents to Cistron.

Immunex said it will take a charge of $18 million to 1996 earnings due to the settlement. The settlement was made without any concession or admission of liability on the part of any party Cistron had sought damages of $26 million to $67 million, plus exemplary damages and attorney's fees under Washington law.

Immunex said it is pursuing claims against its director's and officer's liability insurers for up to $10 million of the amounts to be paid in the settlement. The insurers have disputed the coverage and it said there is no assurance that Immunex will recover the amounts sought.
